newsitem.title: USA: Texaco sued in new discrimination suit.
newsitem.headline: Texaco sued in new discrimination suit.

text.p: A would-be employee sued Texaco Inc on Monday, alleging that the company discriminated against minorities by refusing to hire them.
The suit was filed in Manhattan federal court by Madan Gautan, who is black. The suit seeks class action status.

The case is separate from the widely-publicized 1994 suit brought by a group of black employees who alleged discrimination in pay and promotions. Texaco has proposed a $176.1 million settlement of that suit and a fairness hearing on the accord is set for Tuesday in White Plains federal court.

In the suit filed Monday, the plaintiff alleged that he applied for positions at Texaco, including engineeer, several times over a number of years, most recently, in May and December 1996 and January 1997.

He said that he is an experienced engineer with a bachelor's degree from a foreign university, a masters degree from the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn and credits from the Columbia University Graduate School of Business Administration.
He said that Texaco did not hire him in response to his application because "he is a person of color."

The suit said it is being brought by people who applied for jobs at Texaco between March 17, 1993, and the present but were rejected because of their race. Members of the potential class could number in the thousands, the suit said.
It alleges that Texaco "has and had" hiring practices based on subjective rather than objective job-related criteria that are not uniformly applied to across races.
